setup.task_and_data: Calendar duration questions ('How many days between March 15th and June 22nd?'); accuracy = answer within +-20% of the true duration. Set-A: 365 day-of-year (DOY) x 10 templates = 3,650 prompts for probes and mean-per-DOY activations. Set-F duration prompts: n=332 for the main evaluation (DAS split 232 train / 100 eval); S30 also mentions two halves of 830 prompts (inconsistent with n=332). Held-out template families Set-G (clean acc 0.175) and Set-H (clean acc 0). Cross-task: single-digit addition (n=25), 1D number-line displacement (n=60), country->capital (n=50, excluded because 0% clean accuracy). Off-task collateral prompts: n=60 (arithmetic/trivia/natural) and n=240 (arithmetic/counting/ordinal). Clinical: 979 open-benchmark queries in three tiers (475 synthetic, 133 MedCalc-Bench, 371 PMC case reports) plus a 75-query held-out set.
setup.models: Gemma 2 2B (d=2304, 26 layers; all circuit work), Qwen 2.5 1.5B (d=1536), Qwen 2.5 7B (d=3584), Gemma 2 9B (d=3584), Pythia 1.4B (8 training checkpoints). Nothing above 9B.
setup.positions_layers: Residual stream hook_resid_post at L* = layer with peak monthly-stratified 5-fold CV probe R^2: L*=1 (Gemma 2B), 0 (Qwen 1.5B), 8 (Qwen 7B), 3 (Gemma 9B). Ablation hook at the 'pre-token' (last) position; gradient subspace at last token. Layer sweep of probe-DAS angle over all 26 Gemma layers; DAS energy tracked over all layers and over token positions; MLP/attention ablations at L18-25; head scans over all 208 Gemma heads.
setup.subspaces_compared: Probe U_P: top-k span of a circular (sin/cos DOY) Ridge probe (k=2 default). 'DAS' U_M: k x d orthonormal basis (QR-parametrised) trained 400 AdamW steps to maximise NLL of the correct duration token under the projection-out hook x -> x - U^T U x (this is an ablation-maximising subspace, not interchange-intervention DAS). Also gradient subspace (SVD of dNLL/dh), PCA top-k, INLP, LEACE, Mean-Projection, SAE top-50 features, attribution-patching heads, TFA predictable/novel components.
setup.baselines: Probe ablation; n>=25 Haar-random matched-rank ablations (n=20 at 7B/9B) with 5-95% envelope; PCA, gradient, INLP, LEACE, SAE, attribution patching on one ruler; for the clinical monitor: max-softmax, top-1 prob, top-10 entropy, prompt length, number of date positions.
setup.controls: Analytic Haar null arccos(sqrt(k/d)) plus Monte Carlo (10^4-10^5 draws); whitened coordinates; strict 60/20/20 splits, 5-fold CV, bootstrap, leave-2-template-out; layer sweep; non-linear probe families and alternative probe targets; seed stability (5 seeds, CCA) and k-sweep for effective rank; norm fraction removed by each basis; off-task JS divergence and top-1 agreement; Pythia step-0 probe as decodability baseline; Fieller CIs and additive drops for ratio metrics.

key_results.claim: On Gemma 2 2B at L*=1, ablating the 2-D probe subspace costs ~0.6 pp, while ablating the 4-D 'DAS' subspace takes accuracy from 42% to 0%.
key_results.quote: drops duration accuracy by only 0.6 pp—statistically identical to a random control. DAS ablation at the same layer and same k drops accuracy from 42% to 0%

key_results.claim: The probe-DAS principal angle is indistinguishable from the angle between random subspaces.
key_results.quote: find it indistinguishable from the angle between two random subspaces (the Haar-uniform null), meaning the probe has learned a direction orthogonal to the model's actual computation

key_results.claim: With 1,000 bootstraps the angle CI is [87.28, 88.28] deg; the null 88.3 deg is just outside, so the probe is very slightly but significantly closer than random.
key_results.quote: The Haar null (88.3° ) falls 0.02° outside the upper bound—a statistically significant but geometrically negligible deviation of 0.5°

key_results.claim: Additive DAS drops are 42-51 pp at all four scales; random drops go to zero at 7B/9B.
key_results.quote: DAS drops 42–51 pp while random controls drop ≤0.3 pp at 1.5B and exactly zero at 7B/9B

key_results.claim: Probe-DAS angles at 7B and 9B are not reported in the paper.
key_results.quote: angles on Qwen 2.5 7B and Gemma 2 9B are saved with checkpoint pickles and reported in the released results

key_results.claim: The causal subspace saturates at k=4 and is seed-stable.
key_results.quote: The effective rank of the causal subspace is 4: accuracy drops plateau at k=4, the basin is unique across seeds (CCA>0.94

key_results.claim: Single DAS directions do little in NLL; the full 4-D projection is catastrophic (59x 'cooperation').
key_results.quote: Single-direction ablations yield ∆NLL ∈ [0.08, 0.51] (sum= 1.16); the full k=4 ablation yields ∆NLL = 68.8, a cooperation ratio of 59×

key_results.claim: The DAS subspace is moderately task-specific: duration drop is 12.6x the mean drop on 240 non-calendar prompts (ordinal prompts drop 10 pp).
key_results.quote: the 42 pp duration drop is 12.6× the average across n=240 non-calendar prompts

key_results.claim: DAS ablation also shifts outputs on unrelated prompts (JS ~10x random), though top-1 tokens mostly survive.
key_results.quote: the DAS basis does induce measurable distributional shift beyond a random k=4 ablation on non-date prompts (JS ∼10× the random null)

key_results.claim: Routing is distributed across heads; bottleneck at L11-L12; heads act via QK (attention pattern), not OV.
key_results.quote: single-head ablation has no effect, but the top-10 heads together drop accuracy 17.2 pp, and cascading ablation localizes the routing bottleneck to L11–L12

key_results.claim: Boundary heads route through attention patterns, not value-output writing.
key_results.quote: boundary heads route via attention patterns, not value-output composition

key_results.claim: Late MLPs: probe-aligned writes at L18-19, DAS-aligned writes from L20.
key_results.quote: At L18–L19, probe contribution peaks (4.3× null at L19) while DAS contribution is sub-null; at L20–L25 the pattern inverts

key_results.claim: MLP zero-ablation hurts at every late layer; attention ablation often helps.
key_results.quote: MLP ablation increases NLL at every layer from 18 to 24 (mean ∆NLL= +0.26), while attention ablation is positive only at layers 18–19 and 21

key_results.claim: Attribution patching puts the causal computation at L24, not at L*=1 where DAS is trained.
key_results.quote: The peak is at L=24 (score=1.90); L* =1 has score 0.14 (7th percentile).

key_results.claim: A gradient (first-moment) subspace leans slightly toward the mediator and not toward the probe.
key_results.quote: The gradient subspace sits 2.3° closer to the mediator than to the Haar null (θ̄=85.3° ), while its angle to the probe is at null (88.9° )

key_results.claim: PCA top-4 removes 18.5 pp even though its angle to DAS is near null.
key_results.quote: PCA and Mean-Projection capture 18.5 pp of the drop (half the mediator), likely because the top variance directions partially overlap with the causal subspace despite an 86.8° angle

key_results.claim: Same probe-orthogonal-to-mediator pattern in single-digit addition.
key_results.quote: even for single-digit addition—a purely symbolic task with a perfect probe (R2 =1.0)—the decoded direction is orthogonal to the causally load-bearing subspace

key_results.claim: Probes decode dates even in an untrained network.
key_results.quote: probe R2 =0.956 at step 0—an untrained network “represents” dates by the probe's standard

key_results.claim: The mediator aligns with the context-predictable (TFA) component, not the novel one.
key_results.quote: the DAS mediator aligns 7.1–7.6× more strongly with the predictable subspace than with the Haar-random null, while the probe sits at 88.5°

key_results.claim: Cross-model Procrustes transplant of DAS coordinates fails (population-level, not coordinate-level, universality).
key_results.quote: Rescue recovery was 2.9% of the ablation gap (95% CI [0.7, 6.0]), DOY-shuffled null 0.7%, random-map null 1.5%

key_results.claim: Adversarial two-part perturbation moves DAS coordinates 71 days while the probe readout stays within 5.7 days (Figure 6, text only).

key_results.claim: A confidence 'monitor' probe also sits at the random angle to DAS.

key_results.quote: On Gemma 2 2B, accuracy within ±20% by tier is 10% (A) / 3% (B) / 4% (C)

methods.name: Readout-mediator angle with Haar null
methods.what_it_measures: Mean principal angle (and sum cos^2) between a probe subspace and a causally identified subspace at the same layer and rank, compared with the analytic null arccos(sqrt(k/d)) and a Monte Carlo null.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Fate 2 (bypass): correct answer decodable from a subspace that is geometrically unrelated to the subspace whose removal breaks the answer. Also a cheap first screen for H3.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Ablate each subspace separately with matched random controls; inject along the probe direction vs the causal subspace.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Cached activations plus a trained causal subspace; angle computation is CPU-only.
methods.code_available: Paper refers to 'released code' and cached_tensors paths; no URL appears in paper.txt.

methods.name: Matched-rank random-ablation envelope, additive drop and specificity ratio
methods.what_it_measures: Accuracy drop from projecting out a subspace vs the 5-95% envelope of n>=25 Haar-random subspaces of the same rank; additive drop and Fieller CIs when the random drop is ~0.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Any fate claim that rests on ablation (bypass vs used; override if ablating the competing signal restores the correct answer).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Standard control for every Stage A/Stage B ablation.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: 25+ extra forward passes over the eval set per subspace; cheap.

methods.name: Ablation-maximising subspace search (their 'DAS')
methods.what_it_measures: A k-dim orthonormal subspace (QR-parametrised) trained to maximise NLL of the correct token when projected out at one layer; k-sweep finds where the drop saturates.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Locates where the correct answer is load-bearing; with pressured items, could test fate 3 (not routed: the subspace is used on clean items but carries nothing under pressure) or fate 4 (override: a second subspace for 'agree with user').
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Seed CCA, k-sweep, per-direction ablation, off-task collateral, transfer to held-out templates.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: 400 AdamW steps, batch 8; 4 min (L4) at 1.5B to 42 min (A100-80G) at 9B per model and layer.

methods.name: Gradient subspace
methods.what_it_measures: SVD of per-prompt dNLL/dh at one layer and position; participation ratio; angles to probe and causal subspaces.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Fate 1 vs 2: whether the readout direction lies in the output-sensitive subspace at all.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Ablate top-k gradient directions with random controls.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: One forward+backward per prompt; 332 prompts in 63 s on an L4 (under $1).

methods.name: Subspace energy tracking across layers and tokens
methods.what_it_measures: ||U x||^2 / ||x||^2 vs the k/d null at every layer and token position.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Fate 6 (erased) candidate if energy of the correct-answer subspace falls to null at some layer; fate 3 if energy is present but never reaches the answer position.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Patch or restore the subspace at the layer/position where energy drops.

methods.name: Grassmannian embedding (MDS on mean principal angle) with a random-frame cloud
methods.what_it_measures: Relative positions of many subspaces (from different tools or conditions) against 100 Haar-random frames.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: H1: whether subspaces found under different pressures cluster together or apart.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Cross-condition ablation: ablate the pushback-derived subspace on tempting-option items.

methods.name: QK-twist head scan with permutation null and BH-FDR
methods.what_it_measures: For each head, diagonal-averaged QK scores over an ordered variable (DOY) to find heads that attend at a fixed offset; permutation p-values, BH correction.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Routing heads: by analogy, heads whose QK prefers the user's claim vs the model's own earlier answer (fates 3/4).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Group head ablation with dose-response; cascading ablation by layer group.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Mean activations per value of the variable; CPU/GPU light.
methods.code_available: Algorithm 3 pseudocode; per-head CSV said to be released.

methods.name: Per-direction and combination ablation (cooperation ratio)
methods.what_it_measures: Whether a multi-dim subspace acts jointly (super-additive) or as separable directions.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Whether the correct-answer signal is one direction or a joint subspace (affects whether single-probe monitors can see it, H3).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Choose the minimal intervention rank for Stage B fixes.

methods.name: Collateral and norm controls for ablations
methods.what_it_measures: JS divergence and top-1 agreement on off-task prompts; fraction of activation norm removed by each basis.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Guards against mislabeling 'broke the model' as 'removed the knowledge'.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Required companion to any ablation result.

methods.name: Probe-shift under ablation and two-component adversarial injection
methods.what_it_measures: How much a monitoring probe's readout moves when the causal subspace is ablated or steered while the probe direction is held fixed.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: H3 (probes trained on normal behaviour miss transformed/bypass failures).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Should be paired with measuring the model's actual output change (the paper measures DAS coordinates instead).
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Cached activations plus a few forward passes.

methods.name: Probe on untrained checkpoint
methods.what_it_measures: Probe accuracy at random initialisation as a decodability floor.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Needs an init checkpoint (Pythia-style suites) or re-initialised weights.

methods.name: Manifold deviation score delta(x)
methods.what_it_measures: Residual norm of an activation off the top-k PCA span of reference mean activations (Algorithm 4).

controls_worth_copying: Report additive drop (pp) with a 25-draw matched-rank random-ablation envelope; avoid ratios when the random drop is near zero (they report Fieller CIs showing the ratio is unbounded at 7B/9B).
For every principal-angle claim give sum cos^2 against k1*k2/d with a Monte Carlo null at the exact (d, k1, k2), and repeat in whitened coordinates (activation covariance effective rank was ~11.5).
Angle robustness: strict 60/20/20 splits, 5-fold CV, bootstrap, leave-2-template-out, and a full layer sweep rather than only the selected layer.
Off-task collateral (JS divergence, top-1 agreement on 60-240 unrelated prompts) and the fraction of activation norm each ablation removes.
Seed stability (5 seeds, CCA, pairwise angles) and a k-sweep to locate effective rank (tight basin at k, scatter at k+2).
Decodability floor: probe accuracy on an untrained checkpoint.
Simple baselines for any monitor (prompt length, top-1 probability, top-10 entropy).
Non-linear probe families and alternative probe targets to rule out probe capacity as the reason for a null angle.

pitfalls.pitfall: Their 'DAS' is not interchange-intervention DAS: it is a subspace optimised to maximise the correct-token NLL when removed. Such a search will find something damaging, which shows causal controllability, not that the subspace mediates the duration variable.
pitfalls.quote: DAS mediator subspace (QR-parametrised, trained to maximise ablation NLL)

pitfalls.pitfall: Full DAS ablation breaks output formatting (no integer is produced), so the 0% accuracy may reflect a broken answer format rather than removed duration information.
pitfalls.quote: Clean 39.5%, probe 38.9%, SAE-top-50 28.0% (−11.5 pp), DAS 0% (all first-token integer parses fail under full-DAS ablation)

pitfalls.pitfall: The layer-1 'mediator' looks structural/positional and token-identity-like (copula features, delimiter tokens, month embeddings); Figure 18's per-token energy is nearly identical across prompts. Removing it early may remove inputs rather than a computation.
pitfalls.quote: The mediator subspace at L* =1 encodes positional/structural information (which tokens carry date arguments), not the semantic relation between them.

pitfalls.pitfall: The DAS basis points at month token embeddings.
pitfalls.quote: Projecting the k=4 DAS basis UM onto token-embedding directions, the top cosines are with January, February, March, and their numeric forms

pitfalls.pitfall: At k much smaller than d any two subspaces are near 90 deg, so 'angle at null' is weak evidence; the mean principal angle is insensitive (PCA at 86.8 deg still removed 18.5 pp).
pitfalls.quote: In high dimensions, the answer turns out to be stark: any two low-rank subspaces are nearly orthogonal by default.

pitfalls.pitfall: The authors note that orthogonality does not imply inertness.
pitfalls.quote: orthogonality alone does not imply causal inertness—a subspace can be orthogonal to the mediator and still affect the output through other pathways

pitfalls.pitfall: Specificity ratios are unstable when the random drop is at the noise floor (the same gradient tool appears as 150x, ~21x and 19.1x).
pitfalls.quote: both denominators are in the noise floor, so absolute ρ is sensitive to sampling but the ordering is stable

pitfalls.pitfall: Activations are strongly anisotropic, so isotropic analytic nulls understate variance.
pitfalls.quote: the anisotropy-corrected standard deviation is 14× wider than the isotropic approximation

pitfalls.pitfall: At 7B/9B only DAS-vs-random drops are shown (single runs); probe angles and probe ablations are not in the paper, so 'replicates across scales' is only half-shown.
pitfalls.quote: angles on Qwen 2.5 7B and Gemma 2 9B are saved with checkpoint pickles and reported in the released results

pitfalls.pitfall: Low clean accuracy (42-51% within +-20%); the factual domain was dropped because the 2B model scored 0%.
pitfalls.quote: Gemma 2 2B achieves 0% clean accuracy (n=50 prompts), so ablation metrics are undefined

pitfalls.pitfall: The adversarial 'mechanism shifts 71 days' result is measured in DAS coordinates, not in the model's output, so it is partly true by construction.
pitfalls.quote: mechanism displacement is the nearest-neighbor DOY in DAS coordinates

pitfalls.pitfall: Probe and DAS target different variables: the probe decodes an input (date), the DAS search targets the output (duration NLL); their dissociation is less surprising than framed (reader's note, not stated in the paper).
Internal inconsistency: Fig. 3D shows AP top-24 = boundary set (IoU 1.0) while S5 reports IoU 0.14 at K=24.
pitfalls.quote: Top-K vs. boundary-head set IoU / recall: (K=12) 0.06/0.08; (24) 0.14/0.25

pitfalls.pitfall: Internal inconsistency on where boundary heads are: S4 says none above L15; S46 lists L20 and L23-25.
pitfalls.quote: with a long tail through layer 11; later layers (L>15) carry no boundary heads

pitfalls.pitfall: Second half of the boundary-head inconsistency.
pitfalls.quote: The top-10 boundary heads span layers 1, 11, 12, 20, 23–25.

pitfalls.pitfall: Claimed monotone reliability is contradicted by their own bins (0.96, 0.85, 0.91, 0.95, 0.99).
pitfalls.quote: The wrong-rate is monotonically increasing across δ-bins (Spearman ρ=1.0)

pitfalls.pitfall: Figure 38 caption contradicts the plotted per-DOY shifts (most are well above 3 days).
pitfalls.quote: Per-DOY probe shift under DAS ablation; most are below the 3-day threshold.

pitfalls.pitfall: Null angle misreported (87.6 deg elsewhere for k=4, d=2304).
pitfalls.quote: Across all 26 layers the probe–DAS angle is within 1.5° of the Haar-null (89.6° for k=4, d=2304).

pitfalls.pitfall: delta(x) is described as coming from the mediator subspace, but Algorithm 4 builds it from the PCA of mean DOY activations.
pitfalls.quote: A manifold-deviation score δ(x) derived from the mediator subspace can flag likely errors on clinical duration queries

pitfalls.pitfall: NLL saturation: full ablation gives dNLL ~69 nats, so 'super-additivity' in NLL partly reflects the log scale; one direction (u4) alone causes a large accuracy drop despite 0.7% of the dNLL (reader's note).
Steering comparisons (alpha=3 additive steering) are set against a rank-4 projection, two different interventions; SAE 'zero effect' is about the intervention size/type.

limitations_quote: the DAS basis does induce measurable distributional shift beyond a random k=4 ablation on non-date prompts (JS ∼10× the random null) — these four directions are not literally inert for the rest of the model
limitations_note: There is no dedicated limitations section; this is the closest explicit admission. Other admissions: frontier-scale extrapolation is open (p13), the controlled perturbation test (S38) was not run, an alternative-loss sweep was not run (S29).
future_work_quote: Whether the readout–mediator angle can guide the design of causally grounded monitors—e.g. probes regularized toward the DAS subspace or mediator-aligned circuits as oversight targets—is the most immediate next step

bears_on_fates.how: Direct methodological template: a high-R^2 probe whose removal is harmless, compared against a subspace whose removal is catastrophic, with angles and random-ablation envelopes. Caveat: their probe decodes an input variable and their 'mediator' is an NLL-maximising ablation subspace.
Gradient-subspace check tells whether a readout direction lies in the output-sensitive subspace; not tested on threshold failures.

Layer/token energy tracking, QK head scans and cascading head ablations show how to follow a signal from where it is present to where it is used; the injection test that would directly show 'injecting works' (S38) was proposed but not run.
No competing signal is studied; only the idea that a second optimised subspace could be found.
Cross-model Procrustes transplant failed (population-level but not coordinate-level sharing); suggests a within-model, cross-condition Procrustes test but does not run one.
Subspace energy staying above null at every layer is the kind of test that rules out erasure, though energy is not content.

bears_on_fates.fate: H3 (probes trained on normal behaviour miss failures)
bears_on_fates.how: Mock monitor probe at the random angle and probe-shift-under-ablation tests directly target H3, but the constructions are weak (DAS coordinates as outcome, scalar-energy MI).

bears_on_group_angle: Helps: a full kit for comparing groups of directions as subspaces - principal angles and sum cos^2 with exact Haar nulls, Monte Carlo and whitened versions, Grassmannian MDS against a random-frame cloud, k-sweeps and seed CCA for effective rank, subspace energy across layers and tokens. These transfer directly to tracking the correct-answer subspace across layers/tokens and comparing pressures (H1). Warns: (1) at k << d almost every pair is near 90 deg, so use sum cos^2 against k1*k2/d with matched dimensions (they mix 10-dim and 4-dim subspaces against a 4-vs-4 null); (2) mean angle is insensitive (PCA at 86.8 deg still carried 18.5 pp); (3) anisotropy widens the null 14x; (4) per-token subspace energy is dominated by template position (Fig. 18), so flipped-vs-resisted token paths must be compared at matched positions; (5) an optimised causal subspace can be a generic 'output format' subspace, so add off-task and format checks; (6) cross-model Procrustes failed, so transformed-vs-erased tests should be within one model.
architecture_location: Gemma 2 2B only for the circuit: optimised subspace at L1 (~4% depth) on hook_resid_post; attention 'boundary heads' with a causal bottleneck at L11-L12 (~45% depth) acting through QK patterns, not OV; late MLPs L18-25 (70-100% depth) with the largest zero-ablation effects at L18-19 and L24; attribution patching peaks at L24 (92% depth). Other models: the selected layers are also early (Qwen 1.5B L0, Qwen 7B L8, Gemma 9B L3) because L* is chosen by probe R^2, not by causal search. Cross-model: the +-30/+-61-day offset modes recur in Gemma 2B and Qwen 1.5B (population level), but coordinates do not transfer. Across checkpoints (Pythia 1.4B): head counts and circularness change in a window of 10^3-5x10^4 steps; probe R^2 is high from init. No component-level analysis above 2B.
actionable_fix: Monitoring: do not deploy a probe as a monitor without reporting its angle (sum cos^2) to a causally identified subspace, an additive ablation drop and a random-ablation envelope; the authors suggest (untested) regularising probes toward the causal subspace. Their delta(x) deviation monitor is weak (AUROC 0.63, tied with entropy). For our project: in Stage A, pair every probe-based fate call with ablation of an optimised subspace plus random envelope, off-task collateral and format checks; in Stage B, verify that any probe-based fix target is causally load-bearing before training against it.
reuse_verdict: adapt - copy the measurement and control kit (sum cos^2 with Monte Carlo/whitened nulls, 25-draw random-ablation envelopes with additive drops, k-sweep and seed CCA, off-task collateral, untrained-checkpoint probe floor). Avoid: treating an NLL-maximising early-layer ablation subspace as 'the mediator' without format/off-task checks; specificity ratios; the scalar-energy MI test; the delta(x) monitor; measuring 'mechanism shift' in the subspace's own coordinates.
relevance_to_project: Methodologically relevant to fate 2 (bypass) and H3, and a good source of subspace-geometry controls for the group angle. It is not about acting against known information: no pressure, no flips, small models (1.5-9B; circuit only at 2B) and low clean accuracy. Its headline is weaker than framed because the 'mediator' is an adversarial ablation subspace at layer 1 that breaks answer formatting, the probe decodes an input variable, and several figures contradict the text. Less relevant than its title suggests; use as a methods-and-pitfalls source, not as evidence about fates.
